objectives.text: Find the four embers hidden in the side rooms, then set them in the Gallery lamps in order
Find the three winch gems at the far ends of the long halls to raise the Grotto causeway
Find the miners' sheets and set the Sigil Hall stones
Open the door to the throne and face the Drowned Sovereign

actions.text: The Sovereign's crown cracks. His armour of black water comes apart in one long, rushing sigh, and for a moment the whole hall is silent.
It is down... it is actually down! Chains! Get chains on it before it---
The water in the hall rises. Not a wave: one single breath, drawn back from every corner of the cave.
The tide... remembers you. It has always... remembered...
...Do you hear that? Something in the water is singing. I feel like I have heard it before.
The Sovereign's last surge hits like a falling wall. The party is swept off its feet. Kenji hears Miya cry out his name, and then there is only the sound of the sea.
The Sovereign's last surge hits like a falling wall. The party is swept off its feet, and then there is only the sound of the sea.
Voices, far away. Boots in shallow water.
A Sovereign, in dust. Eight thousand gold of arena beast, and nothing left to chain. I cannot march into the Colosseum with empty hands.
Captain... the swordsman is alive. He brought it down himself, near enough.
Then he is the catch. A fighter who can break a Sovereign belongs in the Pit. The crowd will pay to watch what he can do. Chain him.
No, please, he needs a healer, not chains! Let me tend---
A chapel healer? Good. The infirmary is full of my drowned men. Take her up to the Colosseum. The swordsman goes below.
Kenji! Kenji, stay with me, I will find you!
Darkness, and the long grind of a cart on stone.
The smugglers' road. The chapel's records say their camp lies a little way in, with a fire we can rest at, if it still burns.
Lead on. Or follow, I am good either way. Just do not let me wake any kings.
The third stone settles. A deep chime runs through the hall, and the sigil door grinds open.
The lantern gutters and drops into the water. In the silt beneath it, something glints.
You find
The zealot dissolves into ash. His offering bowl, still full, rolls to a stop at your feet.

npcs.name: Pell
npcs.title: Cave fence
npcs.line: Psst. Everything here was found, not stolen. Browse?

npcs.name: Captain Merrow
npcs.title: Sellsword
npcs.line: Coin buys steel, steel buys time. Looking to hire?

actions.text: Gallery's north of here, past the long hall. The lamps in there want four embers, and the embers are hid in the side rooms. Don't light 'em wrong; the lamps bite.
Captain kept a log on the table by the crates. Read it before you touch a thing.
...the first seal... is mine to keep. Let the dead king's gate stay shut.
The second seal sleeps under my claws. Every light that comes this deep goes out.

npcs.name: Tolliver
npcs.title: Miner-trader
npcs.line: Picks, rope, and a good lantern. What are you short of?

actions.text: The Sigil Hall's north of here. Three crystal stones, and the door won't open until all three show the right colour. Foreman wrote it down. Three sheets, three galleries.
West shaft, east shaft, and the little one off the south passage. And mind the stones: they cycle red, blue, green, gold.
The third seal, and the last. The king's court sleeps. Leave it to its sleep.
You come back to my court? Then draw your blades, and let the sea decide.
The Sovereign is no beast! It drowns the whole floor under us. Help us, swordsman, or we all go under!
Chains... we need chains on its legs. Somebody hit it, anything!
Captain, the net's gone, it tore it like paper!
Captain, the net's gone, it tore it like paper!
A pale lantern drifts out of the dark, swaying. The face behind it is a drowned sailor's.
'The king keeps no guests. Only company.'
A robed figure is kneeling in the dust, whispering the king's name over and over. He rises, slowly, as you approach.
THE HOLLOW CAVE. BENEATH ITS FLOORS THE COURT OF THE DROWNED SOVEREIGN WAS LAID TO REST. THOSE WHO DISTURB IT WILL BE MET IN KIND.
The stone is warm. You feel the cave stir: every guardian you felled stands again, every lamp goes dark, and the sealed ways close behind you.

actions.text: You settle by the fire and feed it a few sticks. Warmth soaks into tired limbs. This is now your save point: if the cave beats you, you will wake here.

'...the Captain had us light the Gallery lamps with the four embers, in the old order, or the roof comes down on the lot of us. Tide first, always. Then the hearth. Then the sun. Moss last. One ember to a lamp, and the lamps bite if you get it wrong. We hid the embers in the stashes round the cave so no one could do it by accident. Hope nobody does.' The rest is smeared with grease.
'DOV WAS HERE. DOV WAS ALSO HERE FIRST.'
'Hid the good rum in the east stash. Hid the better rum under it. Do not tell Dov about the best rum.'
In a crack at the back of the west stash a pale-blue stone glows. You take the Tide Ember. It is warm, and it hums faintly.
Under a pile of rags in the east stash, a red cinder pulses. You take the Hearth Ember. It is warm, and it hums faintly.
The lamp is cold and empty. You have no Hearth Ember to set in it.

FOUR LAMPS, FOUR EMBERS. THE EMBERS ARE HIDDEN IN THE SIDE ROOMS OF THE CAVE. CARRY THEM HERE AND SET THEM IN THE ORDER THE SMUGGLERS KEPT. A WRONG LAMP PUTS ALL FOUR OUT AND WAKES WHAT SLEEPS IN THE WALLS.
On a ledge in the Gallery's west room a golden stone glows. You take the Sun Ember. It is warm, and it hums faintly.
Behind where the Warden stood, a green stone glows in the moss. You take the Moss Ember. It is warm, and it hums faintly.
THE FIRST SEAL IS KEPT BY THE GALLERY'S WARDEN. IT HAS STOOD HERE SO LONG THE ROCK HAS GROWN OVER ITS FEET.

THE CAUSEWAY SLEEPS BENEATH THE WATER. THREE WINCH-GEMS RAISE IT. EACH WAS SET AT THE FAR END OF A LONG HALL: ONE BEYOND THE CAMP'S EAST STASH, ONE BEYOND THE GALLERY'S WEST ROOM, AND ONE BEYOND THE LAKE'S EAST BANK.
The gem sinks under your palm and glows a deep blue. Somewhere far off, stone grinds on stone.
The gem hums. One of the causeway's three winches is awake.
THE WEST WINCH. THE GALLERY'S MASTERS WANTED THE LAKE RAISED ONLY BY THOSE WILLING TO WALK TO THE END OF THE WORLD.
The gem sinks under your palm and glows a deep blue. Somewhere far off, stone grinds on stone.
The gem hums. One of the causeway's three winches is awake.
THE EAST WINCH, BEYOND THE SMUGGLERS' STASH. THE SMUGGLERS NEVER FOUND IT; THEY NEVER LOOKED PAST THE RUM.
The gem sinks under your palm and glows a deep blue. Somewhere far off, stone grinds on stone.
The gem hums. One of the causeway's three winches is awake.
THE LAKE WINCH. THE LONGEST HALL FOR THE LAST GEM.
THE WATER IS COLD AND DEEPER THAN IT LOOKS. THE KING'S MEN WERE ALL GOOD SWIMMERS. THEY ARE STILL DOWN THERE.
THE CRYSTALS SING WHEN THE SEA IS HIGH. THE MINERS CAME FOR THEIR SONG AND LEFT THEIR DEAD BEHIND.
'West shaft is a dead end. Do not let them tell you otherwise. Left a nice big chest for whoever digs through. Be kind. - H.'
THE SECOND SEAL LIES WHERE THE CRYSTALS ARE THICKEST. WHATEVER NESTS THERE FEEDS ON THE LIGHT.

Foreman's tally, sheet one. 'THE LEFT STONE IN THE SIGIL HALL MUST WEAR THE COLOUR OF THE SEA. Put the others wrong and the door just laughs.'
Foreman's tally, sheet two. 'THE MIDDLE STONE MUST WEAR THE COLOUR OF THE SUN. If it turns up red it is only the dust. Turn it once more.'
Foreman's tally, sheet three. 'THE RIGHT STONE MUST WEAR THE COLOUR OF MOSS. Left, middle, right: sea, sun, moss. Then the door. Then the dead. God help the next shift.'
The stone turns and its glow shifts to blue.
The stone turns and its glow shifts to green.
The stone turns and its glow shifts to gold.
The stone turns and its glow shifts to red.
The stone is locked in place, humming softly.

THREE STONES, THREE COLOURS. LEFT, MIDDLE, RIGHT. THE MINERS KEPT THE ORDER ON PAPER, ONE SHEET PER SHAFT. A TURNED STONE CYCLES RED, BLUE, GREEN, GOLD.
THE COURT OF THE DROWNED SOVEREIGN. THEY SWORE TO STAND WITH HIM UNTIL THE TIDE TURNED. THE TIDE HAS NEVER TURNED.
'HERE LIE THE KING'S TWELVE, EACH WITH HIS OWN TREASURE, EACH BOUND TO KEEP IT. IF YOU TAKE IT, TAKE IT QUIETLY.'
BEYOND THIS DOOR THE SOVEREIGN KEEPS HIS THRONE. THREE KEEPERS HOLD THREE SEALS. WHEN ALL THREE HAVE FALLEN, THE DOOR WILL OPEN. ONLY THE BRAVE ENTER.

Steel rings off stone. Beyond the arch, the Sovereign's hall is half underwater: scarlet-and-iron Colosseum guards are scattering across the flooded floor, chains and nets tangled round a colossus of black water and rusted crown.
Hold the line! Nets on its legs! The arena is paying a fortune for this thing alive, so nobody lets it fall!
Captain, it tore the net like paper! The water keeps healing it. We are losing the whole squad!
...I can see that, Dren.
You! Swordsman! Whoever you are, you are the best thing that has walked in here all day. Hit it before it drowns the lot of us!
Hold on. You are trying to capture that? Alive?
Colosseum business. Do you want to argue, or do you want to live?
They are bleeding, Kenji, and so are you if that thing reaches us. I will keep everyone standing. Please, just stop it.
Right. Then I will keep it busy.
Right. Keep your heads down, I will keep it busy.
More mortals. More chains. You come into my court, and you ask me to kneel?
Then draw your blades, and let the sea decide.
THE DROWNED SOVEREIGN
You open the chest and find
You open the chest and find
You open the chest and find
'WE SANK THE KING BENEATH THE TIDE, AND THE TIDE REMEMBERED. LET NO ONE WAKE HIS COURT.'
'HE WAS A GOOD KING, ONCE. THE SEA ASKED FOR A PRICE, AND HE PAID IT WITH HIS PEOPLE.'
'THE BELL IN THE EASTERN HALL RINGS ON ITS OWN. DO NOT ANSWER IT.'
'WHOEVER FINDS THIS: THE LANTERN-BEARERS WERE HIS KEEPERS. THEY ARE BOUND TO THE LAST LIGHT. PUT THE LIGHT OUT AND THEY REST.'
